Key check: after solving Multivariate calibration, explain why at least two wrong approaches fail.

Concept

Multivariate calibration uses several measured variables to predict analyte or sample properties.

Theory

Multivariate calibration uses several measured variables to predict analyte or sample properties. Training and external validation must be separated. Preprocessing and variable selection must avoid leaking validation information into model fitting, especially with highly correlated spectra. Worked case: A near-infrared model trained on spectra from one batch may fail on a new batch with different background variation. Testing held-out batches reveals generalization more honestly than randomly separating repeated scans from the same sample. Interpretation and limits: Do not treat training-set fit as a substitute for independent prediction performance. Application: Multivariate models extract quantitative information from overlapping analytical signals.

Worked case

A near-infrared model trained on spectra from one batch may fail on a new batch with different background variation. Testing held-out batches reveals generalization more honestly than randomly separating repeated scans from the same sample.

Relationship

prediction model maps a vector of responses to a calibrated property

Correction / limitation

Do not treat training-set fit as a substitute for independent prediction performance.

Application

Multivariate models extract quantitative information from overlapping analytical signals.

Key check: after solving Traceability and reference materials, explain why at least two wrong approaches fail.

Concept

Metrological traceability links a measurement result to a reference through a documented chain of calibrations with stated uncertainties.

Theory

Metrological traceability links a measurement result to a reference through a documented chain of calibrations with stated uncertainties. A reference material's assigned value, uncertainty and matrix relevance determine its role. Traceability concerns the result and chain, not simply the brand of the instrument. Worked case: A metal assay checked with a certified reference material should compare the measured and certified values together with their uncertainties. Agreement of rounded central values alone does not evaluate the uncertainty chain. Interpretation and limits: A calibration sticker alone does not establish traceability for every analyte and sample preparation. Application: Reference materials support comparability between laboratories and over time.

Worked case

A metal assay checked with a certified reference material should compare the measured and certified values together with their uncertainties. Agreement of rounded central values alone does not evaluate the uncertainty chain.

Relationship

traceability requires documented references and uncertainty contributions

Correction / limitation

A calibration sticker alone does not establish traceability for every analyte and sample preparation.

Application

Reference materials support comparability between laboratories and over time.

Key check: after solving Measurement uncertainty, explain why at least two wrong approaches fail.

Concept

Measurement uncertainty characterizes the spread of values reasonably attributed to a measured quantity.

Theory

Measurement uncertainty characterizes the spread of values reasonably attributed to a measured quantity. A measurement model identifies contributing inputs and how their uncertainties propagate. Correlations and distributions matter; systematic effects may require correction as well as uncertainty accounting. Worked case: For concentration c = m/V with independent small relative standard uncertainties of 1% in m and 2% in V, the combined relative standard uncertainty is approximately sqrt(1^2+2^2)% = 2.24%. Interpretation and limits: Do not add percentage uncertainties in quadrature when important correlations invalidate the independence assumption. Application: Uncertainty budgets make analytical comparisons and compliance decisions interpretable.

Worked case

For concentration c = m/V with independent small relative standard uncertainties of 1% in m and 2% in V, the combined relative standard uncertainty is approximately sqrt(1^2+2^2)% = 2.24%.

Relationship

independent relative uncertainties combine in quadrature for products and quotients

Correction / limitation

Do not add percentage uncertainties in quadrature when important correlations invalidate the independence assumption.

Application

Uncertainty budgets make analytical comparisons and compliance decisions interpretable.

Chemical Metrology and Quality Assurance · Detection and quantification limitsnew case
Previous worked example

Worked example focus: define analyte, choose calibration, calculate with units, then report uncertainty. Example: standards of 1, 2 and 3 mg L⁻¹ give signals of 0.20, 0.40 and 0.60. A sample signal of 0.50 corresponds to 2.5 mg L⁻¹ from the calibration line, before applying any dilution factor. Key check: after solving Detection and quantification limits, explain why at least two wrong approaches fail.

Concept

Detection and quantification limits describe different levels of analytical capability under specified statistical and practical criteria.

Theory

Detection and quantification limits describe different levels of analytical capability under specified statistical and practical criteria. Detection concerns distinguishing a signal from background, while quantification requires an acceptable level of quantitative performance. A formula based on blank variation and slope is an approximation that must match the validation framework. Worked case: If blank-signal standard deviation is 0.010 units and slope is 0.20 signal units per mg/L, a simple 3-sigma detection estimate is 3x0.010/0.20 = 0.15 mg/L. This does not by itself establish a validated quantification limit. Interpretation and limits: A detectable signal is not automatically quantifiable with adequate precision and trueness. Application: Capability estimates guide method selection and interpretation of low-level analytical results.

Worked case

If blank-signal standard deviation is 0.010 units and slope is 0.20 signal units per mg/L, a simple 3-sigma detection estimate is 3x0.010/0.20 = 0.15 mg/L. This does not by itself establish a validated quantification limit.

Relationship

approximate detection concentration = chosen signal multiplier x blank sigma / slope

Correction / limitation

A detectable signal is not automatically quantifiable with adequate precision and trueness.

Application

Capability estimates guide method selection and interpretation of low-level analytical results.

Key check: after solving Validation and robustness, explain why at least two wrong approaches fail.

Concept

Robustness evaluates sensitivity to small deliberate method variations around intended operating conditions.

Theory

Robustness evaluates sensitivity to small deliberate method variations around intended operating conditions. Changing pH, temperature, flow or timing can reveal vulnerable parameters. Robustness differs from repeatability under unchanged conditions and does not justify arbitrary changes outside the investigated range. Worked case: A chromatography method is tested at nearby mobile-phase pH values. If critical peak resolution collapses after a small pH change, pH control is a robustness concern even when injections at the nominal pH are highly repeatable. Interpretation and limits: High repeatability at one setting does not prove robustness across practical operating variation. Application: Robustness studies define control needs before transferring an analytical method.

Worked case

A chromatography method is tested at nearby mobile-phase pH values. If critical peak resolution collapses after a small pH change, pH control is a robustness concern even when injections at the nominal pH are highly repeatable.

Relationship

deliberate parameter variation tests method stability

Correction / limitation

High repeatability at one setting does not prove robustness across practical operating variation.

Application

Robustness studies define control needs before transferring an analytical method.

Key check: after solving Laboratory quality systems, explain why at least two wrong approaches fail.

Concept

A laboratory quality system organizes procedures, competence, records and corrective actions to support reliable results.

Theory

A laboratory quality system organizes procedures, competence, records and corrective actions to support reliable results. Quality control monitors ongoing performance, whereas validation establishes fitness for a purpose. Deviations require investigation and documented responses rather than automatic deletion of inconvenient data. Worked case: A control-sample result outside a predefined action limit triggers investigation of calibration, reagents and preparation. Reporting only the repeat that passes without explaining the first result defeats quality assurance. Interpretation and limits: A quality system is not merely a collection of certificates or an occasional successful control result. Application: Documented quality practices support dependable analytical services and reproducible research.

Worked case

A control-sample result outside a predefined action limit triggers investigation of calibration, reagents and preparation. Reporting only the repeat that passes without explaining the first result defeats quality assurance.

Relationship

quality assurance links procedures, controls, records and corrective action

Correction / limitation

A quality system is not merely a collection of certificates or an occasional successful control result.

Application

Documented quality practices support dependable analytical services and reproducible research.
